speaker: james_burbage
text: Carve the shoulder, Cuthbert, and send the dish on. Mutton on a Sunday wants no ceremony.

speaker: cuthbert_burbage
text: There is ceremony enough at Greenwich for the whole river. The Earl of Derby marries my Lord Burghley's granddaughter today, and the Queen is there.

speaker: george_bryan
text: It was put off a week. Tilney's office has been sewing for it ever since. A wedding night in a great house goes by a rule, if you have lived in one. A masque after supper. A banquet. The hall cleared at midnight.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: And who plays before them, while the trenchers go out? Is anyone sent for?

speaker: cuthbert_burbage
text: Derby has his own men. If a play goes into that hall tonight, his own livery carries it. That is that.

speaker: will_kemp
text: A bridegroom with his own players saves himself a walk to Whitehall. I have danced for less thrift, and I have been paid later than the garter.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A wedding wants a play as a feast wants a fool, Dick. Something light to get the company to bed.

speaker: james_burbage
text: A wedding wants paying for.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: There. Give him mutton and he furnishes a masque between the salt and the cheese. Dost thou mean to write it down, Will?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Not a word of it. I am not carrying a sentence home in my sleeve to make a play of a supper.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Then I will furnish the moral, since you will not. A wedding is an excellent occasion for paying players who have already been paid.

speaker: george_bryan
text: That is an unusual definition of excellent.

speaker: george_bryan
text: And it is the very match the young Earl of Southampton was said to have paid dearly to refuse. I am not pricing a lord's refusal at this table.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Paid dearly, and no sum. I like a rumour better when it cannot be entered.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Let great lords buy their own no. Our two Christmas plays are still a warrant for twenty pound, and not yet had. I am not spending that money at this table.

speaker: cuthbert_burbage
text: The Chamber pays when the Chamber pays. A harder carve will not open a chest.

speaker: will_kemp
text: I can wait for twenty pound. You might tell me, Master Shakespeare, whether Tuesday's book has a clown in it, since Sunday will not have a play.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Tuesday morning the book is read at Dick's. You are in the company. You are not holding a roll tonight. Abel has the book. No roll left a parlour yesterday, and none leaves this table in a sleeve.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: This table is a supper. Thou wilt not bring me Berowne between the cheese and the door.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not bring thee a part, Dick. Supper is supper. Greenwich is tonight, and we are not sent for.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Then eat. A sentence that is not written down is a sentence I can forget before the fire is raked.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Forget it. The hall at Greenwich will be cleared at midnight whether we have a line for it or not.

speaker: will_kemp
text: I shall remember the paying, and forget the play. That is the better half. You may keep the worse, Master Shakespeare.

speaker: cuthbert_burbage
text: Pass the trencher, before the tablecloth is measured against a fee.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The cloth is safe. Nothing is written down. I am not thinking of a play beyond the sentence.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Then let the sentence die on the road. Thou hast eaten. Derby may keep his own men.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Good. I have had enough of weddings that do not pay, and enough of mutton that does. Finish the shoulder.

speaker: will_kemp
text: I am finished. An excellent occasion, by my definition, and George has already corrected the definition. I can live on a correction.

speaker: george_bryan
text: You can live on it because nobody is writing it into a book. That is the mercy.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: There is no ink in my hand. There will be none on the stair. Good night is the whole of what I am taking away.
